plan.G: Launch three independent research trees with the objectives below. Once research closes, compare only correctly validated candidates measured under the official protocol. Do not assume gains combine: Mother must compile, check, and measure every assembled combination afresh. Independently confirm the leading integrated candidate with five fresh repetitions, alternating candidates, and retain the best independently confirmed program by the official geometric-mean kernel-time objective.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the valid baseline takes a measured mean of 1.8461 ms across three search repetitions, and the kernel performs an all-pairs calculation. Three distinct levers merit independent research: reuse source particles across targets through shared-memory tiling; reduce pairwise arithmetic through an algebraically equivalent acceleration formulation; and balance parallelism against per-thread source reuse through register-blocked output batching and launch geometry. These can be combined later, but their gains may interact. The provided environment identifies an NVIDIA GH200 and NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3; the exact SM is not stated, so the missions avoid assumptions about version-specific instructions. Preserve the one-kernel interface, the allowed files and launch parameters, and all correctness and measurement requirements.

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, develop and measure shared-memory source tiling: cooperatively stage source Particle records and reuse each tile across target threads, with correct synchronization and tail handling. Explore tile geometry and legal shared-memory/block settings within the 49,152-byte limit. Preserve the 28-byte Particle layout, entry point, and full input-size correctness; pass all stated edge cases and oracle/tolerance checks. Judge by the official geometric-mean CUDA-event time for N=4096,8192,16384, not by an assumed bandwidth gain.
children.subject: Shared-memory tiling of source particles

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, explore an equivalent direct-acceleration formulation that cancels the target mass from the force sum, and selectively evaluate reciprocal-square-root/cube arithmetic or other narrowly scoped math changes. Do not enable global fast math. Preserve softening, update order, exact mass output, and valid behavior for coincident positions, extreme positive masses, and zero or negative dt. Validate all required sizes and oracle tolerances before comparing official benchmark timings; retain slower or inaccurate variants as evidence, not candidates.
children.subject: Pairwise force arithmetic and numerical accuracy

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, explore register-blocked output batching: make the kernel honor the configured items_per_block/grid relationship and evaluate a small number of outputs per thread, reusing each loaded source particle across those outputs where beneficial. Tune legal block and items_per_block settings for the three scored sizes. Keep this tree focused on output mapping/register reuse rather than shared-memory staging or a changed force formula, so its results are complementary to the other missions. Preserve complete output and correctness for all required sizes and edge cases; rank by measured geometric-mean kernel time.
children.subject: Register-blocked output mapping and launch geometry

read.query: T2 direct acceleration mass cancellation valid measured

model_interpretation.claim: The parent uses direct acceleration but approximates the inverse-distance cube with rsqrtf; that combined candidate failed one protected case at n=16384. Keeping the target-mass cancellation while restoring sqrtf and the explicit distSq * dist denominator isolates the math change and may improve oracle accuracy without global fast math. It removes target-mass arithmetic from each pair and the final division, but performance is unmeasured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Retain direct acceleration per unit target mass, algebraically canceling target mass from the pair sum and omitting the final target-mass division.","Replace rsqrtf-based inverse-cube arithmetic with sqrtf(distSq) and division by distSq * dist; preserve softening, output mass, and update order."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Combining the validated shared-memory source tile with the measured rsqrtf inverse-distance-cube arithmetic may reduce pairwise work, but their interaction is unmeasured. The controller must compile, check every required case, and measure this integrated program before judging performance.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Preserved the 512-particle shared-memory source tile, 128-thread block, 14,336-byte shared-memory setting, tail guards, and block-wide synchronization.","Replaced sqrtf and division by distSq * dist with rsqrtf(distSq) cubed and multiplication, retaining softening, source order, mass factor, accumulation, and Euler update order."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Two outputs per thread should reuse each source particle's coordinates and mass while halving the number of threads needed for a fixed output count. A 32-thread block with a 64-output tile may expose more CTAs than the previously measured two-output geometries; its single warp per CTA could instead reduce latency hiding. Controller measurements are needed to determine the effect.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Assign two output indices per thread, separated by blockDim.x, so each CTA covers 2 * blockDim.x outputs.","Reuse each source particle's loaded coordinates and mass for both guarded output accumulations while preserving the original force formula and per-output source order.","Set block=32 and items_per_block=64 with shared memory disabled; guard output loading, accumulation, integration, and storage for partial tiles."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The direct-acceleration variant with cached target coordinates built but failed one protected check at n=16384. This candidate restores the baseline force arithmetic and divides by target mass in the original update order, while splitting the source loop around i removes the per-pair self-index check. Since each target still accumulates sources in ascending j order, output should remain equivalent; the performance effect of the changed loop bounds is uncertain and must be measured only after full correctness validation.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Restore the baseline force accumulation and target-mass division, retaining the original softening and Euler update order.","Replace the single source loop with two ascending-index loops over j < i and j > i, eliminating the per-pair self-index check while preserving each target's accumulation order."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Two outputs per thread can reuse each source particle's loaded coordinates and mass. A 64-thread block with items_per_block=128 doubles the CTA count versus the previously measured 128/256 two-output geometry, potentially exposing more SMs for the scored sizes; the lower warps per CTA could instead hurt, so this requires measurement.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Map each thread to two output indices separated by blockDim.x; set block=64 and items_per_block=128 so the kernel output span matches the configured grid tile.","Load each source particle's position and mass once per source-loop iteration, then reuse those values for both guarded output accumulations.","Guard target loads, accumulations, integrations, and stores for partial final tiles; preserve the existing force formula and per-output source traversal order.","Keep shared memory disabled."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Using two outputs per thread can reuse each source particle's coordinates and mass, while a 256-thread block retains more per-block warps than the previously measured 128-thread configuration. Setting items_per_block to 512 matches the kernel's two-output block span; whether this offsets reduced thread-level parallelism must be measured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Map each thread to two outputs separated by blockDim.x, with a per-block output span of twice the thread-block size.","Load each source particle's position and mass once per loop iteration and reuse them for both output accumulations.","Set block to 256 and items_per_block to 512, matching the kernel's output span; retain zero shared-memory allocation and the original force formula."]}
